To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the more a man is masculine, the more he is likely to be sexually attracted to women, (2) the more a woman is feminine, the more she is likely to be attracted to men, (3) the more masculine and feminine a man and a woman are, the more they are likely to be sexually compatible with each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the effects of the collapse of phallocentric ideals and the effects on traditional gender stereotypes?

the way the new sexual ideals have affected the desire of the analyst, the analyst's fantasy, and the way in which the analyst's desire is expressed in the transference and in the countertransference.
the following question: what are the consequences of the new social and cultural ideals on the psychoanalytic treatment of sexual desire?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, as a consequence of the social changes in our time, the phallocratic ideal is no longer a viable fantasy.
the feminine mystique and the masculine mystique are not only the result of a social construction but that they also have a profound impact on the psychic life of the individual.
desire is a function of the lack in the Other, and that this lack can be located at the level of the phallus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
of a psychoanalysis of the desire of the analyst, a psychoanalysis that is not limited to the analysis of the desire of our patients.
we are all, in a way, 'incomplete' subjects and, therefore, we all need a partner in order to complete ourselves.

of an analyst who has been able to work with the new gender stereotypes and the new sexual freedom that they have allowed, and who has been able, at the same time, to work with the traditional phallocratic fantasies that have survived in spite of everything.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analyst's desire is the desire of the other.

the subject of desire is not the one that is the object of the other's desire, and that the subject is always a subject of the Other's desire, that is to say, a divided subject, always already in the realm of language and culture, always already in search of an Other.
the desire of the analyst is the desire of the other, and the desire of the patient is the desire of oneself.
